name: Valero Energy
description: Valero buys crude oil and other feedstocks, refines them in 15 refineries in the US, Canada and the UK (about 3.2 million barrels a day of capacity), and sells gasoline, diesel, jet fuel and other products, mostly wholesale. It earns the refining margin: what the products sell for minus the cost of the crude and other inputs, less operating costs. About 95 percent of revenue is refining; two smaller segments make renewable diesel (through the Diamond Green Diesel joint venture with a Darling Ingredients subsidiary) and ethanol. Profit is cyclical and margin-driven: operating income fell from $11.9B (2023) to $3.2B (2025, after a $1.1B California impairment) and then jumped to $6.9B in the first half of 2026. Valero has closed one California refinery (Benicia, idled April 2026).

gics.note: Conventional GICS label recorded from general knowledge of the standard scheme; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source. SEC SIC code is 2911 (Petroleum Refining) per EDGAR (description 'Petroleum Refining'). Mowgli classification is not set here.

hq.note: P.O. Box 696000, San Antonio, TX 78269 (EDGAR business address); incorporated in Delaware

businessLines.name: Refining
businessLines.how: Wholesale and bulk customers (fuel distributors, retailers, airlines, exporters) pay market-index prices per barrel for products; Valero keeps the spread over crude cost after operating costs and taxes. Driven by crack spreads, refinery utilization, crude discounts and regional supply outages, not by volume alone.
businessLines.description: 15 petroleum refineries plus the marketing and logistics that support them; sells gasolines and blendstocks, distillates (diesel, jet) and other products (asphalt, petrochemical feedstocks, etc.).

operatingProfit.note: After a $1,131M asset impairment on the Benicia and Wilmington refineries (10-K). Share computed against the three-segment sum of $4,258M, before corporate costs of $1,077M.

businessLines.name: Renewable Diesel
businessLines.how: Sells renewable diesel and SAF at fuel prices plus credit value (blenders' tax credit, Renewable Fuel Standard RINs, California LCFS credits); margin is that revenue minus feedstock (fats and oils) cost. Depends heavily on government credits and policy.
businessLines.description: Diamond Green Diesel (DGD): two plants (St. Charles, about 700M gallons a year of renewable diesel; Port Arthur, about 470M gallons) turning animal fats, used cooking oil and vegetable oils into renewable diesel, naphtha and neat sustainable aviation fuel. Joint venture with a subsidiary of Darling Ingredients, consolidated by Valero.

revenue.note: External; total incl. $2,089M intersegment sales to Refining is $4,597M

businessLines.revenueNote: External; total incl. $2,089M intersegment sales to Refining is $4,597M

businessLines.name: Ethanol
businessLines.how: Sells ethanol to fuel blenders (including Valero's own refining segment) and distillers grains to livestock feeders at market prices; margin is that revenue minus corn and natural gas costs.
businessLines.description: Ethanol plants that make ethanol and distillers grains from corn.
